entities.summary:
The International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), founded on July 13, 1966, in New York City, is a global religious organization rooted in the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and the philosophy of Gaudiya Vaishnavism. Spearheaded by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, ISKCON emerged during a period of cultural upheaval in the 1960s, marking a pivotal moment in the introduction of Eastern spirituality to the Western world. Its establishment represented a significant cross-cultural exchange, influencing both religious practices and social movements globally.

The movement gained momentum in the 1970s, particularly with the opening of its first temple in San Francisco and the publication of numerous translations and commentaries on sacred texts. By the end of the 20th century, ISKCON had established temples in over 70 countries, illustrating its rapid expansion and the increasing global interest in Hindu philosophy. The organization is known for its contributions to vegetarianism and environmental sustainability, as well as its public outreach efforts through festivals, food distribution programs, and educational initiatives.

The legacy of ISKCON is profound, as it has not only revived interest in Hindu spirituality in the West but also led to the establishment of various cultural and educational institutions worldwide. The movement has influenced interfaith dialogues and has inspired numerous offshoots and adaptations of its core teachings, reaching audiences beyond traditional Hindu communities. Its impact is seen in the growing acceptance of Eastern philosophies in Western societies and the integration of religious practices into popular culture.
